texts: On day 121 of Year 1, the wraith approached a lit lantern on the West Row.
The wraith drained mire-essence from the lantern.
The drained lantern gave weak mist-light for the rest of the night.
The weak mist-light attracted a handful of nightmoths.
The wraith persisted for eleven days.
The wraith drained six lanterns on the West Row during its persistence.
Keepers counted about six nightmoths at each drained lantern during the persistence.
The thread harvest at the West Row fell sharply during that week.
The West Row is a lantern-row on the Cliff Path near the Sunken Cove.

q1_issues.issue: "gave weak mist-light for the rest of the night" is rendered as (End sk_give_1 night), which states the giving ended at night rather than lasting the night's remainder, and silently drops the "rest of" restriction.
"during that week" is resolved to the eleven-day persistence eventuality, asserting a temporal containment the text never states — no week-denoting antecedent exists anywhere in the passage.

(CardinalityPhrase (sk_nightmoths $x) "about six") puts a hedged exact number into the slot the instruction set reserves for numberless canonical vague phrases ("several", "a handful", "dozens"), so no seeded rule can map it to a bound.

q2_gaps: extent adverbial naming the remainder of a time period ("for the rest of the night") — RestOf covers entity/mass partitives, duration Measure needs a count, and Start/End take calendar terms, so no licensed carrier exists
degree adverb on a verb ("fell sharply") — the instruction set itself states it has no licensed slot and must be left out
anaphoric temporal NP at a granularity the antecedent never supplies ("during that week") — term propagation has no week-level term to copy

approximate/hedged count ("about six nightmoths") — Cardinality's magnitude is specified as a native integer and CardinalityPhrase is for phrases with no number; the ParticleFromNormal approximation is defined only for Measure
ordinal/continuous day-count date in a non-Gregorian calendar ("day 121 of Year 1") — the Time terms assume a Gregorian Day-of-month inside a Month
review.notes: No CONTEXT block was supplied, so q3 is na. The "each drained lantern" universal is ranged over the six-lantern group of the previous sentence, which silently excludes the first lantern (asserted drained, never asserted a member of that group).

issues.reason: Core patterns bars dropping a stated restriction ("an unencodable qualifier never becomes an unqualified assertion"), yet "the rest of" is dropped and what remains, (End sk_give_1 night), is the Intervals section's "until Y" storage — the giving stopped when night came, roughly the converse of its spanning the night's remainder.

No word in the passage denotes a week, and the Time section forbids inventing a term the antecedent does not supply, so (During sk_fall_1 sk_persist_1) asserts containment in the eleven-day persistence that "during that week" does not state — you cannot point at the words that put that atom there.

Hedged counts are genuinely uncovered (Cardinality's magnitude is a native integer and ParticleFromNormal is defined only for Measure/clock magnitudes), and (CardinalityPhrase sk_nightmoths "about six") is a true, well-typed surface record of the phrase actually used — the calibration line licenses such improvisation, and failing to match a seeded lexicon string is the coverage gap the reviewer separately (and rightly) filed, not a parse defect.

gaps_confirmed: extent adverbial naming the remainder of a time period ("for the rest of the night") — no licensed carrier: Start/End take time terms, Measure duration needs a count, RestOf needs an entity/mass whole
degree adverb on a verb ("fell sharply") — the instruction set itself states such adverbs have no licensed slot and must be left out
anaphoric temporal NP at a granularity the antecedent never supplies ("during that week") — term propagation has no week-level term to copy
approximate/hedged count ("about six nightmoths") — Cardinality's magnitude is a native integer and CardinalityPhrase is specified for phrases with no number
ordinal/continuous day-count date in a non-Gregorian calendar ("day 121 of Year 1") — the Time terms assume a Gregorian Day-of-month inside a Month
new_gaps: "during <time-period NP>" has no head at all when the period is neither an eventuality nor a stated calendar term: During requires two reified eventualities and Time requires a term, so a licensed form would need a period-denoting term at week granularity (a Week/Quarter-style constructor) plus a containment head that accepts a period rather than an event

no head expresses "for the remainder of period P": RestOf ranges over entity/mass wholes, and a time period can never be an entity here (deictic and day-part times are bare constants and the Time section forbids minting an sk_ witness or Member atom for one), so a licensed form would need an interval whose Start is the event's onset and whose End is the period's own end
adjudication.defect_summary: For "for the rest of the night" no compliant form is licensed — the give event should carry its class, roles and Past and no extent atom at all, with the extent recorded as a gap, since End/Start, Measure duration and RestOf each fail on a time period. For "during that week" the compliant form is likewise no temporal atom: with no week-denoting antecedent there is nothing to propagate, and no head may substitute the persistence eventuality for the week.
adjudication.notes: The parse also omits the per-member distribution rule that Cardinality mandates for a counted plural with a distributive predicate ("drained six lanterns"), which the reviewer did not file. The reviewer's note about "each drained lantern" ranging over the six-lantern group is a defensible narrowing, not a defect — an (And (Member $x lantern) (Member $x drained)) range would also have been licensed.
